newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: King Hussein urges Israel to halt settlements.
newsitem.headline: King Hussein urges Israel to halt settlements.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein on Friday criticised a U.S. House of Representatives motion seeking President Clinton's reaffirmation of Jerusalem as Israel's undivided capital, saying it somewhat undermined the U.S. role in Middle East peace efforts.
But Hussein said he hoped the United States would be an "honest broker" in the peace process, adding that Russia and other Western states should also have a voice.
He was speaking to reporters in Geneva after addressing the annual meeting of the International Labour Conference.
In his speech, Hussein called on Israel to halt its "policies of settlement, land confiscation and demographic manipulation", saying they endangered hopes of achieving peace.

Israel, which captured Arab East Jerusalem in 1967 and annexed it in a move unrecognised by the international community including the United States, has welcomed the 406-17 vote by the U.S. House of Representatives in favour of the non-binding resolution.
The vote came as Egypt struggled to resolve a peacemaking crisis between Israel and the PLO spurred by Israel's beginning work in March on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Hussein, on a four-nation European tour this week, said of Tuesday's vote: "I think it is very sad, very unfortunate that such a decision should have emanated from the United States at this particular point in time.
"Jerusalem is a very, very sensitive issue. At the same time it is a final status negotiation issue," he added, referring to negotiations between Israel and the Palestinian Authority.
"This is something for them to decide. To prejudge the issue in this way is not very constructive at all."
Hussein said holy places like Jerusalem had to be above sovereignty. "Beyond that, Jerusalem has to be the symbol of peace between the Palestinians and Israelis. Both of them have equal rights..."

The Jordanian leader said he hoped that Washington would play more than a postman's role. "I certainly hope that the United States will be an honest broker and will contribute more than the airing of views from one side to the other.
"Certainly the United States has a tremendous role to play.
"Unfortunately such actions as we have seen (on Tues) sort of undermine that capability," he added.
In his speech to the International Labour Conference, Hussein said that, under any peace agreement, Jerusalem should be an "open city", whose final status would be determined by the parties.
After capturing Arab East Jerusalem, Israel declared all of the holy city its "eternal and indivisible" capital. The PLO wants East Jerusalem as the capital of a Palestinian state.

In October 1995, the U.S. Senate and the House passed the Jerusalem Embassy Act which states as a matter of U.S. policy that Jerusalem should remain "the undivided capital of Israel" and the American embasssy should be moved there by May 1999.
But it allowed Clinton to suspend the embassy's move from Tel Aviv for six-month periods.
Hussein said Jordan had met its obligations under its 1994 peace treaty with Israel and would continue to work for peace.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has proposed moving immediately into final-status talks that would tackle issues such as Jewish settlements and the future of Jerusalem.

But Palestinians, who have accused the right-wing leader of trying to avoid handing back more occupied land under interim peace deals, have demanded that Netanyahu stop the East Jerusalem project before full-fledged talks can resume.
